newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: TELSTRA SIGNS HUGE INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY DEAL
Australia's largest information technology outsourcing deal has been finalised, with the signing of agreements by Telstra, IBM and Lend Lease Corporation.
Telstra will join IBM Australia and Lend Lease as an equity partner in IBM Global Services Australia to expand its business in the Asia-Pacific region.
Telstra will provide some communications services to IBM Global Services, which will in turn take responsibility for Telstra's data centre operations.
As part of the deal, about 2,100 Telstra employees and contractors will join IBM Global Services.
The alliance will also create a new communications network services company, called Advantra.
MINISTER URGES FAIR DEAL FOR ANR EMPLOYEES
Federal Transport Minister John Sharp has urged the board of Australian National Rail to ensure its employees get their full entitlements when the company is sold.
Bids for the company close today, and Mr Sharp said a winning bid should be chosen by the end of August.
He said some employees who began working for Australian National after 1990 won't be eligible for the employer superannuation contributions as they might have expected.
The minister has told a meeting of the board in Alice Springs that those workers should not suffer when the company passes into private hands.
"We ought to be generous to those people and look at their situation with a degree of sympathy rather than just being strictly technical about it," he said.
BANK MERGER PLAN APPROACHES FINAL HURDLE
All but one hurdle has been passed in the planned merger between Westpac and the Bank of Melbourne.
Today, the Federal Treasurer, the Reserve Bank and the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission all said they would not oppose the $1.4 billion merger.
However, it still has to be approved by Bank of Melbourne shareholders.
Commission chairman Professor Alan Fels said the Victorian operations of both banks would be managed under the Bank of Melbourne logo.
He said the entire Victorian market would be more competitive when Westpac opened access to its electronic banking systems.
NEW FEDERAL SEAT TO INCORPORATE NATIONAL PARTY STRONGHOLDS

The redistribution of Queensland's federal electorates has seen the creation of a new seat called Blair which will take in strong National Party territory, including the shires of Kingaroy and Nananago.
It draws on parts of the existing divisions of Oxley, Fisher, Groom and Longman.
The seat of Rankin has also been affected, with the suburb of Inala now in the new Oxley electorate.
The draft plan will be open for public comment for the next month.
TWO MEN APPEAR IN COURT ON HEROIN CHARGES
Two men have appeared in a Sydney court charged in connection with the importation of 24 kg of heroin, hidden in furniture imported from Malaysia.
Police said the heroin seized has a street value of around A$25 million.
Chee Wah Ho, 43, a toy manufacturer from Hong Kong, has been charged with being knowingly concerned in the importation of a prohibited import and with possessing a prohibited import.
Bin Pang, 28, a taxi driver from the Sydney suburb of Belmore, has been charged with attempting to possess a prohibted import.
Customs officers allegedly detected the heroin inside cavities within a marble table sent in a consignment of 15 crates from Malaysia.
Neither man has sought bail and the matter has been adjourned until next Friday.
FITZPATRICK RATED A GOOD CHANCE TO PLAY TEST
New Zealand rugby union captain Sean Fitzpatrick is now rated a good chance of playing in tomorrow night's test against Australia at the MCG.
Fitzpatrick, who has a knee injury, trained overnight and pulled up OK this morning but was a little sore.
Coach John Hart said a final decision would be made just hours before the match.
"He never ceases to amaze me," Hart said. "There's got to be a chance he does play -- more chance than I thought."
Meanwhile, Hart has launched a blistering attack against Australian coach Greg Smith.
Hart said he was extremely disturbed by comments attributed to Smith that the Wallabies would take matters into their own hands if All Black illegalities were not policed by the referee.
He said the coments did nothing for the game.
